events.title: Simon de Montfort's Parliament Meets
events.description: Simon de Montfort summoned representatives from English towns and counties to the Palace of Westminster. They joined the barons and clergy in a parliament.
events.significance: Historians regard this assembly as a forerunner of the House of Commons. It was an early step toward representative government in England.

events.title: The American Civil Liberties Union Is Founded
events.description: A group of activists that included Roger Baldwin, Crystal Eastman and Helen Keller founded the ACLU in New York. They wanted to defend individual rights during a period of wartime and postwar crackdowns.
events.significance: The ACLU became one of the most influential legal advocacy groups in the United States. It has been involved in many landmark cases on free speech, equality and due process.

events.title: The Wannsee Conference
events.description: Senior Nazi officials met at a lakeside villa in Berlin to coordinate the implementation of the so-called Final Solution. The aim was to organize the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews.
events.significance: The meeting shows how the Holocaust was organized as a bureaucratic, state-run operation. It remains a central document of Nazi genocidal planning.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Is Inaugurated
events.description: At age 43, John F. Kennedy was sworn in as the 35th U.S. President. In his inaugural address he urged Americans to ask what they could do for their country.
events.significance: Kennedy was the youngest person elected president. His speech became one of the most quoted in American history and captured the optimism of the early 1960s.
